newsitem.title: USA: Dow hits record again at bonds' expense, dollar down.
newsitem.headline: Dow hits record again at bonds' expense, dollar down.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average surged to a second consecutive record close on Tuesday as investors withdrew funds from the bond market to join the stock rally.
The dollar fell broadly while the British pound soared after Britain raised interest rates and set a plan to make the nation's central bank independent.
The Dow rose 10.83 points to 7,225.32, surpassing the previous day's record of 7,214.49, and setting its 17th high for the year.
Analysts said the market was caught in cross-currents as some investors rushed back into stocks, while others cashed in profits from the recent surge.
Despite the record finish, stocks clearly lacked the sizzle that sent a bevy of Wall Street records toppling just a day ago.
"The action today was indicative of the market's split personality," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management.
"The technical condition of the market remains outstanding and the breadth has been impressive in recent sessions," Crane said. "But then on the other hand, we've come a long way."
Market breadth was neutral, with advancing issues and declines running in a near dead heat, as 1,260 stocks rose while 1,266 fell.
But the modest rise in the Dow masked a frenzied day in terms of volume. On the New York Stock Exchange, volume topped 601 million shares for only the seventh time in history.

Analysts said the brisk recovery in stocks after the plunge of 700 points in the Dow index between March 12 and April 11, had rekindled interest among investors eager to hop back on an apparently resurgent bull market.
But they also cautioned that near-term gains were likely to be limited at these again lofty levels.

"I do feel the bulk of the near-term gains are probably already in the market, and that's looking both technically and rationally," said Joseph Barthel, chief investment strategist at Fahnestock & Co.
The 30-year Treasury bond fell 5/32, or $1.56 on a $1,000 bond, raising its yield to 6.89 percent from 6.88 percent at Monday's close. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
The dollar dropped to 1.7235 German marks from 1.7330 late Monday, and to 125.40 Japanese yen from 126.60.
The pound jumped to $1.6330 in late trading from $1.6230 late Monday. Higher British interest rates make pound-based assets more attractive to investors.

Grain prices fell as corn planting in the Midwest continued at a rapid pace and better weather in the plains states helped the winter wheat crop battered by a freeze three weeks ago. At the Chicago Board of Trade, corn for May delivery closed 4-1/2 cents a bushel lower at $2.88-1/2.
Speculators also bailed out of the wheat market as supply concerns eased. Wheat for May delivery closed 11-1/4 cents a bushel lower at $3.94, its first close under $4 in a month.

Overseas, London's FTSE 100 Index closed 63.7 points higher at a record closing level of 4,519.3. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average jumped 666.17 points or 3.41 percent to finish at 20,180.92, the highest closing level since 20,413.46 set on Dec. 17.
